guides.title: Enrolling your child in Fair Lawn Public Schools
guides.body:
New students register online. Students already enrolled in Fair Lawn do not need to re-register each year. The Fair Lawn Community School office handles all registration questions.

- Kindergarten pre-registration opens in January (it opened January 21, 2026 for 2026-27). Children must turn 5 by October 1 of the school year.
- Pre-registration for grades 1-12 opens in mid-May (May 13, 2026 for 2026-27). Pre-registrations submitted before the opening date are denied.
- Collect and scan the required forms before you start: proof of residency, district medical forms, a records request (grades 1-12), and if needed the landlord affidavit (Form 214) or Forms 218 A & B. The forms are on the District Registration page.
- Complete the online pre-registration through the district's Genesis portal at www.fairlawnschools.org/openreg once it opens.
- Then email your child's name and incoming grade to flcs@fairlawnschools.org. Staff will review and contact you.
- Kindergarten families are invited to an in-person orientation in late spring or early summer.

Preschool: the district's Integrated Preschool Program at Thomas Edison School (37-01 Fair Lawn Ave) runs five days a week in AM or PM sessions. Online registration opens in spring (April 30, 2026 for 2026-27), and places are limited and first-come.

After you register, the email you gave is used to create your Genesis Parent Portal account automatically. In the portal you can update contacts and report absences. Questions: genesis@fairlawnschools.org.

Community School office: 5-01 Bergen Ave. Open Mon-Fri 8:30am-3:30pm, closed 12-1. Phone (201) 794-5450 ext. 2369, email flcs@fairlawnschools.org.

County high school options: 8th graders who live in Bergen County can apply to the Bergen County Technical Schools (Bergen County Academies, Bergen Tech Teterboro/Paramus, Applied Technology HS, Career Innovation HS). The application opens September 1 of 8th grade, open houses run in October-November, and the BCA deadline is early November (November 8 in 2026).

guides.title: School year essentials
guides.body:
Calendar: the 2026-2027 calendar is on the district site (https://aptg.co/pMPrPn). Students start Tuesday, September 8, 2026, and the school year has 183 student days. FLHS graduation is June 23, 2027.

- Schools are closed Sept 21 (Yom Kippur), Nov 3 (Election Day, students only), Nov 5-6 (NJEA), Nov 26-27 (Thanksgiving), Dec 24-Jan 1 (holiday recess), Jan 18 (MLK Day), Feb 15-16 (Presidents' Day recess), Mar 10 (Eid al-Fitr), Mar 26 (Good Friday), Apr 19-23 (spring recess) and May 31 (Memorial Day).
- Early dismissals: Nov 10 & 12 (PK-4 conferences), Nov 25, Dec 23, Jan 11, Feb 24-25 (K-4 conferences), Mar 15 and June 22-23.
- Snow days: if makeup days are needed, school opens on April 19, then April 20, then April 21.

Weather and emergency alerts: the district sends closings, delays and emergency messages by phone, email and text through SchoolMessenger, usually by 5:45am. Messages go to every phone and email listed for Guardian 1 and 2, so keep your contacts current in the Genesis portal. Closings are also posted on fairlawnschools.org, Facebook, X/Twitter (@FairLawnSchools), Instagram (@fairlawnschools), FOX 5, WABC 7 and News 12 NJ. Please don't call the police for school updates. The free Fair Lawn Schools mobile app is available on the App Store and Google Play.

- Delayed opening start times: elementary 10:10am, middle 9:55am, high school 9:25am. No before care, and no breakfast at FLHS.
- Early dismissal times: elementary and middle 12:45pm, high school 12:35pm. No lunch is served, and after care may be canceled.

Lunch: fund your child's account online at PaySchools Central (payschoolscentral.com), or send cash or a check payable to "Fair Lawn BOE - Cafeteria Account". Unused balances roll over. Menus are at fairlawnschools.nutrislice.com. Free and reduced-price meal applications are on the district website. Food Service Director: 201-794-5470 ext. 4516.

Busing: FLHS and Thomas Jefferson MS have subscription busing (register online, and students need a bus pass). On delayed openings, pickup is 90 minutes later. Transportation Dept: 201-794-5522 ext. 6603.

Board of Education: regular meetings are usually the 4th Thursday at 7:30pm in Room 19 at Thomas Edison School, 37-01 Fair Lawn Ave. Some months the location or time changes. The October 29, 2026 meeting is at the Memorial Middle School Media Center at 7:00pm. Agendas are on BoardDocs, and meetings stream on YouTube. Email the board at boardmembers@fairlawnschools.org.

Flyers from schools and community groups are posted on Peachjar.

guides.title: Summer in Fair Lawn: camps & Memorial Pool
guides.body:
Fair Lawn has two separate sets of summer camps: one run by the school district's Community School and one run by the borough's Recreation & Parks Department. Both register through Community Pass, under different accounts and links.

School district camps (Fair Lawn Community School):
- Camp Sycamore for grades K-3, Camp FLAIR for grades 4-8, and the Counselor in Training program for grades 9-10.
- Registration opens on Community Pass (register.communitypass.net/fairlawn). 2027 dates have not been announced.
- Every camper needs a physical form completed by a physician and submitted at least one week before their session.
- An optional camp lunch program can be added through your Community Pass account.
- Questions: summer@fairlawnschools.org or (201) 794-5450 ext. 2369.

Borough Recreation camps:
- Registration usually opens in mid-April (April 13 in 2026), in person at the Community Center (10-10 20th St) or online via Community Pass (residents only).
- Registration after the June deadline costs a $50 late fee, and there are no refunds once a session starts.
- The Summer Basketball Camp for kids entering grades 2-8 costs $95 (grades 4-8, mornings) or $75 (grades 2-3, afternoons).
- Questions: (201) 796-6746.

Memorial Pool & Spray Park:
- Residents need a membership and a photo ID badge. Register on Community Pass, or in person at the Community Center to pay by cash or check.
- 2025 rates were adult $150, junior $100, senior (62+) $25 and family $300. 100% disabled veterans join free, and veterans/active military get 50% off. Watch the pool page in spring for 2027 rates.
- The pool office ((201) 927-4702) is only staffed in season.
- The Riptide summer swim team practices at the pool and has no tryouts. Swimmers must be pool members.

Other summer fun: Summer Concert and Summer Movie series from Recreation, the district's Summer Music Enrichment Program, and an April Vacation Mini-Camp (info expected February 2027).

guides.title: Youth sports signup
guides.body:
Most youth sports in Fair Lawn are run by Fair Lawn All-Sports (FLAS), a volunteer nonprofit that works with the Recreation Department. A few programs are run directly by Recreation or by independent groups.

Fair Lawn All-Sports (fairlawnallsports.com):
- Sports: soccer (rec plus tryout-based travel), baseball, softball, boys' and girls' basketball, boys' and girls' lacrosse, track & field, wrestling (junior clinic) and kickball. STARS serves the special-needs community.
- Register on the 'Register to Play' page, which uses SportsEngine. Use one email address for the whole family.
- Sign up for FLAS email updates to hear when each season opens. Girls' winter rec basketball 2026-27 registration is open now.
- Volunteer coaches must complete the FLAS coach registration, a background check and Rutgers S.A.F.E.T.Y. certification.
- Contact: fairlawnallsports@gmail.com, or Recreation at 201-796-6746.

Run by Recreation & Parks:
- Street Hockey League for grades 1-12. Register in person at the Recreation Dept. (Community Center, 10-10 20th St, Mon-Fri 8:30-4:30), October 13 - November 13, 2026. Games start in December at Memorial Park.
- Riptide summer swim team at Memorial Pool.
- Summer Basketball Camp (grades 2-8).

Run by other groups:
- Football: Fair Lawn Football Association (fairlawnfootballassociation.sportngin.com).
- Fee-based after-school leagues and clinics through the Fair Lawn Community School: basketball, soccer, fencing, pickleball, golf, tennis and volleyball (Community Pass).

Ice hockey: we did not find a Fair Lawn-based youth ice hockey club. Families typically use clubs at nearby rinks.

guides.title: Programs for seniors
guides.body:
Fair Lawn Senior Center, 11-05 Gardiner Road (corner of 11th St), one block from the library and Borough Hall. Phone (201) 796-1191.

- Open to adults 60+. Membership is free: stop in and fill out an application. Non-residents use a separate form.
- Call to set up a tour with a trained Ambassador and pick up a Welcome Packet.
- A new calendar of events comes out each month, and there is a monthly email newsletter.
- Lunch is served weekdays at noon. Check in by 11:50am and reserve at least 24 hours ahead. The suggested donation is $1.25 for ages 60+ and $6.55 for guests under 60, and there is no take-out.
- Homebound residents can get Meals on Wheels through the Bergen County Division of Senior Services.

Getting around: the borough's free Mini Bus serves residents 18+ within Fair Lawn, weekdays 9am-4pm. Call 201-794-5327 up to two weeks ahead and no later than 3pm the business day before. Other options: Bergen County Transportation (201-368-5955 or 201-336-7400), and Access Link for people with disabilities (800-955-2321, option 1).

More to do:
- The Community Center (free for residents) has a walking track, fitness room, pickleball, table tennis, a Bridge Club (Mon & Thu afternoons) and a card room.
- The library hosts book clubs, ESL and language classes, concerts and art talks.
- Seniors 62+ got a $25 Memorial Pool membership in 2025.

guides.title: Library & lifelong learning
guides.body:
The Maurice M. Pine Free Public Library is at 10-01 Fair Lawn Avenue (201-796-3400). Hours: Mon-Thu 10am-8pm, Fri-Sat 10am-5pm, Sun 1-5pm. It belongs to the BCCLS consortium, so one card works at libraries across Bergen County. You can apply for a card online.

- Kids: Baby Time, Book Buddies, Story Explorers, Homework Help (grades K-8), Lego Club, D&D and reading clubs.
- Adults: ESL (beginner, intermediate and conversation), Spanish classes, book clubs, board game club, concerts, art talks and free legal clinics.
- Other services: museum passes and hotspots to borrow, mobile printing, NJ MVC practice tests, and the Pine Gallery.
- Event calendar: bccls.libcal.com/calendar/fairlawn (subscribable as iCal or RSS).

Adult and continuing education: the Fair Lawn Community School runs after-school and evening classes for youth and adults (dance, yoga, pickleball, SAT prep and more). Browse the course guide and register on Community Pass. Recreation & Parks also offers adult fitness and leisure programs at the Community Center. Community theater: the Old Library Theatre performs at the Community Center Theater.
